full_judgment:
4. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filling written statement denying all the material statements made in the plaint. His case, in short is that the suit is false, baseless, imaginary, malafide, collusive without cause of action not maintainable. The suit is barred by the principles of estoppels, waiver and acquiescence. It is also hit by misjoinder and non-joinder of parties. Admittedly, Shamser @ Samaruddin was the owner of the suit land, who sold the entire .93 acre of land to Alfaf Bepari from plot No. 158 by a registered deed of sale dated 23.02.1922 and handed over possession thereof. The registered deeds of sale dated 08.03.1926 and 02.03.1948 are false, fraudulent and ineffective. Alfaf Bepari died leaving behind seven sons and two daughters; they inherited the property and possessed the same jointly. After that, they made an amicable partition Abdul Jabbar, predecessor of defendant Nos. 2-6, got .19 acre of land in his share and (purchased .74 acre of land from other co-sharers on 31.08.1979 by a registered deed of sale and became owner of the entire .93 acre of land but because of his ignorance the land was wrongly recorded in the name of Shamsher. After that, Abdul Jabbar sold .33 acre of land out of .93 acre from eastern side of the plot to Abdul Malek and others. After death of Safaruddin, his son Nayeb Ali claimed ownership of the property. Abdul Jabbar filed Title Suit No. 683 of 1981 for declaration of title. Nayeb Ali received summons and contested the suit by filing written statements. Then he abandoned the Suit and Abdul Jabbar got an ex parte decree. The plaintiffs never possessed the suit land and the deeds of sale are mere paper transactions. Abdul Jabbar got his name mutated in the khatian and paid rent to the Government and became owner of .32 acre of land. After that, Abdul Jabbar sold the same by a registered deed of sale dated 12.08.1996. This defendant got his name mutated in his purchased land in Miscellaneous Case No. 1202 of 1996 and paid rents to the Government. The plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 191 of 1996 in respect of .93 acre of land before Assistant Judge, Second Court, Narayanganj with a prayer for permanent injunction. The defendant contested the suit by filing written statements and the plaintiffs filed a Violation Miscellaneous Case No. 54 of 1.996. This defendant filed written objection and the suit was dismissed for default on 20.05.1998. Ultimately, the plaintiffs withdrew the suit on 28.07.1998. The defendant constructed 5.50 feet high brick wall surrounding .20 acre of land and installed iron gate. He further constructed boundary wall surrounding 12 plots and erected shed made of corrugated iron and sank tube well and constructed dinning room, bath room and caretaker room. Md. Siddique Miah has been living there with his family members. So, the suit is liable to he dismissed with cost. 

 14. The High Court Division quoted the salient findings of the appellate Court and came to the finding that the plaintiffs could not show that there was misreading or non-reading of the material evidence by the appellate Court occasioning failure of justice and as such, affirmed the judgment of the appellate Court.
